comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims (C1-C15). Both evaluations find these well-established facts about the LC-NE system to be supported by citations and treat them as accepted foundational context.

Perfect agreement on novelty and scope claims (C16-C20, C78). Both evaluations recognize this as the first comprehensive transcriptome map of human LC and praise the resource value and complementary methodological approaches.

Agreement on tissue identification claims (C21-C23). OpenEval also includes validation procedures (C103-C106) which peer reviewers address in R18. Both find the neuroanatomical approach rigorous and appropriate.
Overlap on validation procedures (C103-C106). Both evaluations support the tissue identification and quality control methods as standard and appropriate.
Agreement on SRT methodology (C24-C28). Both evaluations accept the Visium platform approach and experimental design without criticism, recognizing awareness of technological limitations.
Agreement on snRNA-seq methodology (C29-C30, C91). Both evaluations support the FANS enrichment approach and complementary use of technologies as reasonable given technical challenges.

Agreement on annotation and QC procedures (C31-C36). Both evaluations accept manual annotation and quality control approaches, recognizing that spatial resolution limitations were compensated by complementary methods.

Partial overlap on QC procedures (C35-C36). OpenEval finds the sample-specific QC justified but notes the unconventional approach of not filtering mitochondrial reads. Peer reviewers don't specifically address this QC decision in R5.

Strong agreement on SRT differential expression results (C37-C41, C85). Both evaluations find the identification of known NE marker genes validates the approach and confirms expected findings from rodent studies.

Agreement on cross-species comparisons (C42-C43). Both evaluations accept the finding of partial conservation and recognize species differences as important, with appropriate caveats about technological and biological differences.
Partial overlap on snRNA-seq QC (C44). OpenEval finds QC procedures standard, while peer reviewers in R8 express concerns about data quality and sample imbalance.

Both address high mitochondrial content (C45, C49, C92-C93) with UNCERTAIN evaluation. OpenEval notes the unconventional approach may affect data quality. Peer reviewers express concern about 'questionable quality' and sample imbalance in snRNA-seq data.

Overlap on clustering methodology (C46-C48). OpenEval finds the approach appropriate with validation by marker genes. Peer reviewers in R8 express broader concerns about snRNA-seq data quality affecting overall results.

Agreement on snRNA-seq differential expression (C51-C54, C80, C84). Both evaluations support these findings, recognizing the convergence between SRT and snRNA-seq as validation and the identification of potentially human-specific genes as valuable.
Agreement on cross-species snRNA-seq comparisons (C55-C56, C82). Both evaluations accept the findings and appropriately explain differences between single-nucleus and spatial data resolution.

Divergent evaluations on 5-HT neuron identification (C57-C60). OpenEval finds this well-supported by marker genes and UMAP visualization. Peer reviewers urge 'great caution' due to technological limitations and potential for accidental inclusion of adjacent regions.

Divergent evaluations on 5-HT spatial distribution (C61-C64). OpenEval finds RNAscope validation provides strong orthogonal evidence. Peer reviewers remain cautious about interpretation despite validation, citing technological limitations.
Agreement on inhibitory neuron clustering (C65-C67, C135). Both evaluations support the identification of 14 subpopulations and find consistency with rodent studies strengthens confidence in results.

Divergent evaluations on TH+ cell identity (C68-C71, C81). OpenEval finds strong evidence these are NE neurons based on minimal DA marker expression and RNAscope validation. Peer reviewers express significant concern about cell type identification, suggesting results may be over-interpreted and nomenclature should be reconsidered.

Divergent evaluations on cholinergic marker expression (C72-C74, C97-C99). OpenEval finds the observation well-validated by RNAscope showing cellular co-localization. Peer reviewers urge 'great caution' due to technological limitations and potential for technical artifacts or misinterpretation.

Strong agreement on data accessibility (C75-C77, C140-C141). Both evaluations strongly praise the data sharing practices, with peer reviewers calling the user-friendly application 'an enormous asset to the community.'

Partial overlap on main findings summary (C79-C85). OpenEval finds summary claims supported by detailed results. Peer reviewers in R6 validate known marker genes as expected, treating this as validation of the approach.
Partial overlap on summary findings (C80, C84). Both evaluations support the convergence of findings across methods and identification of enriched genes as valuable contributions.

Partial overlap on validation methods (C83). Both evaluations recognize orthogonal validation as a methodological strength, with peer reviewers noting complementary approaches compensate for spatial resolution limitations.

Agreement on disease-relevant genes (C86-C88). Both evaluations support the identification of these genes in human LC-NE neurons as important for understanding disease mechanisms, with appropriate citations to prior literature.

Agreement on spatial resolution limitations (C89). Both evaluations explicitly acknowledge this limitation, with peer reviewers noting it greatly reduces the impact of spatial technology and prevents successful unsupervised clustering.
Partial overlap on FANS justification (C91). OpenEval finds the justification supported by citation to prior work. Peer reviewers accept the methodological choice without challenge.

Partial overlap on small NE neuron count (C90). OpenEval finds this honestly reported with plausible explanations. Peer reviewers express concern about the small number as part of broader data quality issues.

Agreement on uncertainty about 5-HT neuron origin (C94-C96). Both evaluations find the authors appropriately acknowledge uncertainty, presenting balanced discussion while noting the unexpected nature of the finding.

Agreement on ethical procedures and sample characteristics (C100-C102). Both evaluations find ethical approvals and sample selection appropriate and standard, without challenging these methodological details.

OpenEval evaluates analytical methods and metrics definitions (C123-C127, C139) as supported and appropriate for reproducibility. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific methodological details.
